I am playing Monopoly as player p2.

I have no monopolies and cannot build. I am weighing trade offers against p1 and p3.

p4 owns light blue monopolies with four houses each and St. James Place, which blocks my orange monopoly. I previously rejected p4's $600 offer for St. Charles Place. Unowned properties include MEDITERRANEAN, ELECTRIC_COMPANY, STATES, VIRGINIA, NY AVE, KENTUCKY, ILLINOIS, B&O, MARVIN_GARDENS, NC, and PA.

I rejected p3's $450 offer for Indiana. I will stay liquid and buy Kentucky, Illinois, B&O, and Marvin Gardens to block p3. I will not mortgage early or sell Tennessee. I am deciding whether to trade again or end my turn. Boardwalk with three houses costs $1400, which I cannot cover even with full mortgages.

Mortgaging all four properties yields $380, bringing total cash to $1076. That still cannot cover the $1400 Boardwalk rent. I can pay the $500 Park Place and $450 light blue rent with cash alone. From Free Parking, the next spaces are Kentucky, Chance, Indiana, Illinois, B&O, Atlantic, Ventnor, Water Works, and Marvin Gardens.

I rejected p4's $600 offer for St. James Place. Trading Tennessee for it would give p4 two-thirds of the orange monopoly and remove my blocker. Indiana is unlikely to interest p4 because they lack red properties. I will end my turn.

I am reconsidering p4's offer. A single yellow property would block their monopoly, but they might not accept it alone. I also looked at p1, who is cash poor and owns only mortgaged land, so trading with them seems unhelpful.

I will end my turn. I have exhausted reasonable trade options this turn. Staying liquid for Kentucky, Illinois, B&O, and Marvin Gardens is the priority. More trade proposals would leak strategy or annoy opponents.

I am reconsidering a trade with p4. I could offer Pennsylvania Railroad and cash for St. James Place. The orange monopoly is very strong because it lands six to nine times from jail. I would need New York Avenue to complete the set.
